title: [v0.92.1][corporate][sidecar] Finish post-move-in operational control-plane hardening
body:
## Summary

Track the corporate operational hardening gaps discovered during #497 / Sprint 4 closeout as a sidecar issue. These items are useful and important follow-up work from the AWS move-in / corporate control-plane transition, but they do not block the corporate IP-transfer acceptance for #497.

## Background

Issue #497 and PR #613 assembled the CORP-C evidence packet for corporate IP-transfer acceptance. Review found that several operational control-plane readbacks were being treated as #497 blockers: GitHub/CI authority, DNS and certificate ownership, AWS account guardrails, private custody receipt, and deployment rollback readback. The operator clarified on 2026-09-02 that these are sidecar operational hardening items, not blocking conditions for corporate IP-transfer acceptance.

## Scope

- Reconcile GitHub organization/repository/CI authority readbacks into an explicit corporate operational-control record.
- Prove or repair DNS hosted-zone ownership, certificate renewal ownership, and deployment rollback readback for the public corporate surfaces.
- Complete AWS business-account guardrail readbacks for auditability, including CloudTrail, AWS Config, IAM Access Analyzer, account recovery/break-glass posture, and billing/contact custody where appropriate.
- Produce a redacted private-custody receipt proving corporate recovery is not controlled by one personal factor.
- Preserve existing read-only observations from #497 as seed evidence, without treating missing hardening proof as #497 acceptance failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The sidecar issue records the full operational-control denominator separately from #497's IP-transfer acceptance denominator.
- [ ] Each GitHub/CI, DNS/certificate, AWS guardrail, private custody, and rollback-readback item is either proven with retained readback evidence or explicitly decomposed into a narrower follow-on with owner/action.
- [ ] The final evidence distinguishes corporate IP ownership acceptance from operational control-plane hardening.
- [ ] No credentials, account IDs, secrets, private custody artifacts, or sensitive recovery details are printed, committed, or exposed.
- [ ] Any live cloud or account mutation is separately authorized and recorded before execution.

## Non-Goals

- Do not reopen #497 solely for these hardening items.
- Do not claim the hardening gaps are already fixed.
- Do not mutate AWS, GitHub administration, DNS, certificate, billing, or custody settings without explicit scoped authorization.
- Do not block Sprint 4 closeout on this sidecar unless a separate sprint policy explicitly makes it release-blocking.

## Links

- Related to Sprint 4 corporate acceptance closeout.
